naszeProjekty.heading: Nine events. Nine different energies.
naszeProjekty.intro: We do not want to describe projects as a list of names. Each has its own rhythm, audience and reason to exist — from the first day at university to the symbolic close of a degree.

adapciak.desc: Eight days before the academic year begins, first-years meet the people with whom they will soon enter university life. The programme includes team activities, shared challenges and themed evenings — but its real outcome is arriving on campus on day one without feeling anonymous.
adapciak.signature: The first network of friends forms before the first lecture.

animalia.desc: A charity project created to help protect endangered species. It combines an event at Wrocław ZOO with an evening format for students, while funds raised support animals cared for by the ZOO's DODO Foundation.
animalia.signature: Entertainment has a measurable result here: direct support for a specific species.

bal.desc: A joint initiative of the University authorities and the Student Government, bringing students, staff, alumni and friends of UEW into one room. The evening strengthens ties to the Alma Mater, while the ‘Ekonomka’ awards let students recognise people who matter to the university community.
bal.signature: One night in which different generations of UEW meet at the same table.

dni.desc: Talks and training explain the unfamiliar language of university life: the difference between a test and an exam, the Dean's role, how course completion works and where to find room to grow. Formal knowledge meets social integration so that starting university is not a solitary reading of regulations.
dni.signature: Instead of assuming a new student will ‘somehow find out’, we reveal the system from the inside.

graduetion.desc: A ceremony for graduates inspired by academic traditions associated with American universities. Gowns, caps, diploma presentation and a shared cap toss turn the administrative end of study into a moment worth remembering.
graduetion.signature: A diploma becomes a shared rite of passage, not a document collected from a window.

mosty.desc: A four-day exchange between students of five economics universities, developed since 2005. Lectures, workshops, meetings and case studies offer a first-hand view of how students learn and organise at other academic centres.
mosty.signature: Sometimes the shortest route to a new perspective runs through another university.

test.desc: An inter-university initiative of five student governments in the Forum of Economic Universities. Around one hundred participants at each university enter the qualifying stage, and the strongest represent their cities in a final combining economics knowledge with event-scale competition.
test.signature: Economics leaves the exam room and becomes a community event.

tedx.desc: A local stage for ideas worth spreading, created in the TEDx format. Speakers have a few intense minutes to challenge a familiar assumption, reveal a new phenomenon or leave the audience with a question that keeps working long after the event.
tedx.signature: Not a conference full of slides — one stage and ideas designed to stay with you.

party.desc: A party series for UEW students and the wider student community of Wrocław. It creates a regular space to rest, meet and celebrate beyond classes, projects and examination periods.
party.signature: A community needs shared celebration as much as shared work.

naszeProjekty.joinLead: Behind every event is a team, schedule, partners, production, communications and dozens of decisions invisible to participants. Join the delivery team or support it as a partner.

prawaStudenta.heading: Every student has the right to know their rights
prawaStudenta.intro: Under the Higher Education Act, every student has the right to training on their rights and duties. The student government organises this training together with the Students’ Parliament of the Republic of Poland.

repeat.title: Repeating classes
repeat.desc: The right to repeat certain classes in the event of unsatisfactory academic results, on the terms set out in the university regulations.
repeat.expl: If you fail a subject, you have the right to repeat it under the study regulations — you’re not automatically expelled.

ios.title: Individual study plan
ios.desc: The option to apply for an individual study plan — flexibly adapting the curriculum to your needs.
ios.expl: Do you work, train competitively or have another important life situation? You can apply for a flexible plan and individual assessment dates.

absence.title: Excused absence
absence.desc: The right to excuse an absence and take leave from classes, including sitting exams at another date.
absence.expl: Illness or an important life event? You have the right to excuse an absence and sit the exam at another date.

change.title: Changing your field of study
change.desc: The Act allows you to change your field of study while following set procedures.
change.expl: Feel it’s not the right field? You can change it, and subjects you’ve already passed will be recognised under the procedure.

ects.title: Transferring and recognising ECTS credits
ects.desc: The right to transfer and recognise ECTS credits from other universities — domestic and foreign — in line with mobility rules.
ects.expl: Credits earned at another university, including abroad (e.g. Erasmus), can be recognised — you don’t pass the same thing twice.

commission.title: Board exam
commission.desc: The right to take a board exam, with an observer of your choice present.
commission.expl: Disagree with an exam grade? You can request a board exam, and an observer you choose has the right to be present.

mode.title: Changing your study mode
mode.desc: The option to transfer between full-time and part-time studies, in line with the university regulations.
mode.expl: Has your situation changed (e.g. work)? You can move from full-time to part-time studies or vice versa, under the regulations.

source.q: Where do my rights as a student come from?
source.a: From the Higher Education Act (Ustawa 2.0) and the UEW study regulations. The Act guarantees, among other things, the right to training on students’ rights and duties.

ios.q: What is an individual study plan (IOS)?
ios.a: It’s the option to flexibly adapt the curriculum and organisation of your studies to your situation. You apply for it on the terms set out in the university regulations.

commission.q: Can I take a board exam?
commission.a: Yes. You have the right to a board exam, with an observer of your choice present.

report.q: Where do I report that my rights are being broken?
report.a: Contact the Student Ombudsman — they’ll help interpret the rules and, if needed, represent you before the university’s units.

correction.title: Updated from the PDF Infopack
correction.body: The PDF states fixed limits of three courses and 25 ECTS. The current §40 contains no such figures — it asks the Dean to assess whether the ECTS deficit is excessive and whether other obstacles apply.

absence.label: Absence from class or an exam
absence.title: An absence must be explained within a set time
absence.summary: The teacher excuses a short absence from class or an assessment; an examiner handles an exam absence. The reason is assessed using documents provided by the student.
facts: You provide the teacher with the reason and documents within 14 days after the reason for absence ends.
For an examiner, the deadline is 3 days after the reason for absence ends.
Once accepted, the examiner sets an individual exam date and the teacher defines how missed work is made up.
The Dean excuses an absence from a diploma exam and sets a new date.

supplementary.label: Supplementary courses
supplementary.title: Check your study programme first, then the registration date
supplementary.summary: The Infopack rightly gives humanities, social-science, language and PE courses their own chapter. Their exact number and semester depend on the programme for a particular course of study, while the Regulations define how registration works.
facts: Check the programme assigned to your course, degree level and year of entry for the courses that apply to you.
Registration for courses and course groups takes place in USOS on dates set by the Dean.
Foreign-language registration is managed by the Foreign Languages Centre.
Registration dates must be announced at least 2 weeks before registration opens.

grades.label: Grades and percentage thresholds
grades.title: The same grading scale applies to assessments and exams
grades.summary: The Regulations connect each numerical grade with the achieved learning outcomes. When points are used, points may not be deducted for a wrong answer or no answer.
facts: 5.0: at least 90%; 4.5: 80% to under 90%.
Programmes with external accreditation may apply the accrediting institution’s requirements.

exams.label: Assessments, exams and results
exams.title: Dates and results should not arrive as a surprise
exams.summary: The Regulations set minimum notice periods for assessments and exam schedules, as well as deadlines for grades. Students must also check their grades in USOS.
facts: A graded assessment other than an exam must be announced at least 2 weeks in advance.
Exam dates must be published no later than 4 weeks before the session starts.
An assessment result is due within 2 weeks; an exam result within 3 days.
A negative grade must be communicated no later than 3 days before the resit.
Check final USOS grades within 7 days after the resit session ends.

conditional.label: Conditional progress or repeating a semester
conditional.title: Conditional progress is a Dean’s decision, not an automatic limit
conditional.summary: If you have not passed the semester, you may request conditional progress or permission to repeat it. The Regulations leave the assessment of an acceptable ECTS deficit to the Dean.
facts: Submit the request within 10 days after the resit session ends and all grades are in USOS.
A request for conditional progress or semester repetition does not require justification.
Conditional progress may be allowed if the Dean considers the ECTS deficit not excessive and no programme or legal obstacle applies.
As a rule, the same semester or course may not be repeated more than twice.

leave.label: Leave from classes
leave.title: Leave may be short- or long-term
leave.summary: At a student’s request, the Dean may grant leave when participation in classes is temporarily impossible. In some cases, selected courses may still be taken during leave.
facts: Short-term leave lasts up to one month; long-term leave generally lasts two semesters and exceptionally one.
Reasons include health, education or research, pregnancy or parenthood, financial hardship or a sudden serious event.
Apply immediately after the reason arises; leave cannot be granted for a completed semester.
The Dean may indicate courses to be completed during leave.

registration.label: Course registration
registration.title: Registration takes place in USOS on dates set by the Dean
registration.summary: The Regulations distinguish registration for an individual course from a course group. Foreign-language classes are registered separately by the Foreign Languages Centre.
facts: Registration dates must be announced at least 2 weeks before registration starts.
If you miss an individual course registration through no fault of your own, you may ask the Dean to enrol you.
If you do not select a course group, the Dean assigns one ex officio.
Leaving a course you registered for requires the Dean’s consent.

applications.label: Applications and individual matters
applications.title: A good application starts with a specific request
applications.summary: As a rule, the Dean decides individual student matters. Before submitting an application, the Regulations advise checking the relevant rules and consulting the Dean’s Office.
facts: The application should contain a concise request and substantive — and where possible formal — justification.
Attach the documents required for the matter and supporting the facts in your justification.
You receive at least 7 days to correct missing elements; failure to do so leaves the application unexamined.
A simple decision should be issued within 14 days; a matter requiring clarification generally within one month.

diplomaLive.metaDesc: Check your APD and defence readiness, understand JSA, deadlines and reviews, and estimate the weighted graduation result at UEW.
diplomaLive.heroLabel: From the final grade to your defence.
diplomaLive.heroTitle: You are not uploading a file. You are closing a process.
diplomaLive.heroLead: A thesis in APD is only one of several gates. This cockpit shows what submission really means, where the process can stop and what your next move is until the defence.

readiness.label: Readiness cockpit
readiness.heading: Find the first real blocker
readiness.lead: Select only conditions that are actually complete. The result does not assess your thesis — it orders dependencies and identifies the next step.
readiness.privacy: The state stays only in this browser tab. Nothing is stored or transmitted.
readiness.completeBody: Confirm the date and committee in APD. This result does not replace a supervisor's or UEW administration's decision.

grades.title: All courses and grades are in USOS
grades.body: Your curriculum is complete and no missing grade blocks admission.
grades.action: Check USOS and resolve every missing grade. Uploading the thesis alone does not count as submission.

promoter.title: Your supervisor accepted the final version
promoter.body: This is the APD-ready version, not an earlier working file sent for comments.
promoter.action: Confirm with your supervisor that this exact version is approved for upload to APD.

finance.title: Your obligations to the University are settled
finance.body: There are no outstanding fees or unresolved obligations blocking the process.
finance.action: Check payments and electronic clearance in USOS; ask the Dean's Office about any uncertainty.

apd.title: Metadata, declaration and file are in APD
apd.body: Title, abstract and keywords are complete in Polish and English, and the thesis was sent to the supervisor.
apd.action: Complete PL/EN metadata, accept the declaration, upload the correct file and send it for approval.

jsa.title: The JSA report was assessed by your supervisor
jsa.body: The PRP colour does not make a decision. Your supervisor reads the report and accepts the thesis or requests revision.
jsa.action: Wait for the report and supervisor decision. A thesis may undergo no more than two JSA checks.

reviews.title: Two positive reviews and clearance are complete
reviews.body: Reviews by the supervisor and reviewer plus University clearance open the path to the exam.
reviews.action: Check reviews and clearance in APD/USOS. Reviews should be available at least 2 working days before the exam.

approval.title: Green light 1 · APD
approval.body: Your supervisor accepted the thesis and sent it for review in APD.

grades.title: Green light 2 · USOS
grades.body: USOS contains every grade required by your curriculum. You need both green lights at once.

timeline.label: Process map
timeline.heading: Six states, not one upload
timeline.lead: Every state has a different owner and risk. Do not plan the defence as if everything happened instantly after upload.
timeline.mapNote: This is a responsibility map, not a copy of the APD interface. Select a stage to see its owner and the evidence that the process has actually moved on.
timeline.proofLabel: How to know this stage is complete

final.title: Final version
final.body: The supervisor confirms that a specific file may enter the formal process.
final.proof: The supervisor has clearly approved this version for submission, rather than merely sending another round of comments.

metadata.title: APD and metadata
metadata.body: You complete PL/EN data, accept the declaration and send the thesis to the supervisor.
metadata.proof: APD shows a complete thesis record, the correct file and a status confirming transfer to the supervisor.

similarity.title: JSA screening
similarity.body: APD sends the thesis to the national anti-plagiarism system and generates a report.
similarity.proof: A similarity report is attached to the thesis; the percentage alone does not yet mean approval.

decision.title: Supervisor decision
decision.body: The supervisor analyses the report, accepts the thesis or requests changes.
decision.proof: The thesis status confirms acceptance after JSA analysis or clearly requests a revision.

reviews.title: Reviews and clearance
reviews.body: Supervisor and reviewer submit reviews and the University confirms clearance.
reviews.proof: APD contains two reviews and University clearance no longer blocks admission to the exam.

defence.title: Diploma exam
defence.body: The date and three-person committee appear in APD at least 7 days in advance.
defence.proof: APD shows the date, place and three-person diploma examination committee.

deadlines.label: Deadline navigator
deadlines.heading: Choose your route
deadlines.lead: Primary dates come from the 2025/2026 Infopack. Final deadlines were checked against the current process rules.
deadlines.warning: Missing the final deadline may result in removal from the student list. If you are near the boundary, do not rely on this page alone — contact your supervisor and the Dean's Office.

jsa.label: JSA lab
jsa.heading: Colour is a signal, not a verdict
jsa.lead: PRP helps the supervisor read the similarity report. It does not automatically assess authorship and cannot replace source analysis.
jsa.rule: The current rules allow no more than two JSA checks. The supervisor decides within 3 working days after receiving the report.

green.title: The report still needs to be read
green.body: A low PRP does not end the analysis. The supervisor checks where similarities come from and whether quotations and borrowed material are marked correctly.

orange.title: Similarities require careful analysis
orange.body: The result signals a larger share of similarity. The supervisor assesses its nature and decides whether the thesis proceeds or needs revision.

red.title: A high PRP requires a supervisor decision
red.body: This is a serious signal, but still not an automatic verdict. Do not try to ‘lower the percentage’; work with sources and supervisor feedback.

exam.label: Defence table simulator
exam.heading: Three people. Three angles.
exam.lead: The oral exam includes three questions. Instead of studying everything in the same way, prepare a separate strategy for each question type.
exam.notice: The date and committee should appear in APD at least 7 days before the exam.

chair.title: Can you place your thesis in the wider context of your programme?
chair.body: The question comes from the published topic list for your programme. It checks orientation in the discipline, not just recall of one definition.
chair.prepare: Work through the 40 or 50 topics and prepare a definition, relationships and one example for each.

promoter.title: Do you understand the concepts your thesis is built on?
promoter.body: The supervisor asks about the theoretical part, conceptual choices and literature. It tests understanding of your argument, not recitation of a chapter.
promoter.prepare: Explain the main concepts without quoting the text and justify why the chosen theory fits the problem.

reviewer.title: Can you defend the method, result and limitations?
reviewer.body: The reviewer focuses on the research problem, method, results and conclusions — including what the study does not prove.
reviewer.prepare: Practise a 90-second answer: objective → method → key finding → meaning → one limitation.

calculator.label: 60/20/20 calculator
calculator.heading: See what really weighs on the result
calculator.lead: Enter your study average, two thesis grades and three oral-exam grades. The calculator applies the proportions described in the Infopack.
calculator.disclaimer: This simulates components and weights, not the official diploma grade. UEW determines the final result and its classification under the applicable rules.

goal.label: What do you want to gain?

mode.label: How do you like to work?

circles.rhythm: Meetings and projects vary by circle

choir.title: Ars Cantandi Choir
choir.summary: Regular rehearsals, voice training, concerts and trips. Reading music and prior experience are not entry requirements.

mobility.rhythm: Recruitment and preparation, then an intensive stay

dthub.title: DT HUB
dthub.summary: Workshops and project teams across university, business and institutions — for people who want to research needs, prototype and facilitate change.

career.title: Careers Office and JobTeaser
career.summary: Career planning, mentoring, training and job, internship and traineeship offers. Start with a consultation or a JobTeaser profile.

kafe.title: K(A)FE and micro-credentials
kafe.summary: A free 2–3 month competence programme with workshops, learning materials, DT Innovathon, digital badges and UEW micro-credentials.

commitment.label: The cost of saying yes
commitment.heading: Ask before you join
commitment.lead: Recruitment usually tells you what you gain. A good decision also requires knowing what you may have to give up.

hours.question: How many hours is a normal week, and a week before an event?
hours.why: An average without peak periods hides the real load.

firstTask.question: What is a new member's first task?
firstTask.why: A concrete example reveals onboarding culture better than ‘dynamic team’.

peak.question: Which months are most intense?
peak.why: Compare them with exams, work, internships and your energy.

exit.question: Can I try one meeting or leave after one project?
exit.why: A low exit cost lets you test fit without guilt.

start.label: First experiment
start.heading: Do not commit blind
start.lead: Design thinking instead of deciding by logo: a small experiment, real contact, then commitment.

observe.title: Observe the current channel
observe.body: Check recent work and whether the group is alive, not merely listed.

contact.title: Ask one specific question
contact.body: Ask about the next meeting, first task and real work rhythm.

trial.title: Run a small trial
trial.body: Choose an open meeting, training, choir rehearsal, workshop or one project.

decide.title: Assess your energy afterwards
decide.body: Do not only ask whether it was fun. Ask whether you want to return to these people and this work.

current.title: K(A)FE plans its next recruitment in August 2026
current.body: The current DT HUB page describes a free 2–3 month programme with workshops, DT Innovathon, digital badges and micro-credentials. It shows why a living guide cannot stop at PDF content.

libraryLive.metaTitle: Library without getting lost — living guide
libraryLive.metaDesc: Find a book, choose the right pickup route, access digital resources remotely and handle UEW Library tasks step by step.
libraryLive.heroLabel: The catalogue tells you where. This guide tells you what next.
libraryLive.heroLead: The catalogue tells you a book exists. This guide tells you what happens next — where to find it, how to collect it, when to use the Book Locker and how to reach databases off campus.

source.label: Access map
source.title: Library Infopack + current UEW Library pages

task.label: Need navigator
task.heading: What do you need to do?
task.lead: You do not need to know the Library structure or service names. Choose an outcome to get the shortest path and the right source.
task.rule: Hours, availability and charges can change. For those details, we always open the current Library page.

register.label: Create an account
register.title: Register online, then activate your account
register.summary: Registration starts in the catalogue form. Then visit the Circulation Desk to confirm your details, activate the account and encode your student ID.
steps: Complete the online registration form.
Visit the Circulation Desk within 14 working days.
Activate the account and encode your student ID.
register.note: After activation, your barcode and QR code are also available in the Library account.

find.label: Find a book
find.title: First the record, then call number and location
find.summary: Search by title, author or subject. In item details, note two things: call number and location. Together they trigger the correct route.
steps: Search for a title, author or subject in the catalogue.
Open details and save the call number and location.
Use the item router below to choose your pickup method.
find.note: Books are ordered by call number on shelves. If you get stuck, ask a librarian on any floor.

borrow.label: Borrow or renew
borrow.title: The borrowing route depends on location
borrow.summary: An item from closed stacks must be ordered first. A floor item is usually found by yourself. A standard student account allows 10 books for 3 months.
steps: Check the item's location and status.
Order it or find it on the correct floor.
Collect at the desk, Book Locker or use Selfcheck.
borrow.note: Limits may differ for double-degree students and student organisations. Renewal depends on your account conditions.

return.label: Return a book
return.title: A return does not need to wait for opening hours
return.summary: During opening hours, return the book on a floor. Otherwise, use the 24/7 return box at the main entrance from Wielka Street.
steps: Check whether the Library is open.
Return on a floor or use the 24/7 return box.
Check your account once the return is processed.
return.note: No student ID is needed for the return box. The Book Locker is for pickup, not returns.

digital.label: Access e-resources
digital.title: Direct on campus, through proxy off campus
digital.summary: Find databases, journals and e-books in Library e-resources. Outside the UEW network, configure the current proxy file and sign in with your university account.
steps: Find a database or publication in e-resources.
Off campus, configure proxy using the current instructions.
Sign in with your university account and follow the licence.
digital.note: Licences prohibit systematic mass downloading. Download only what you need for your own study or research.

study.label: Reserve a workspace
study.title: Choose a zone or reserve a study cabin
study.summary: The first floor suits group work; the third is the quietest. Floors 2 and 3 have 14 cabins: 8 individual and 6 group rooms.
steps: Match the zone to the kind of work.
Reserve a cabin no earlier than one week ahead.
Arrive on time and confirm use.
study.note: A booking may be cancelled after 30 minutes of absence. Students can book no more than one week ahead.

clearance.label: Complete Library clearance
clearance.title: Settle all Library obligations first
clearance.summary: Before clearance, return all loans, pay accrued charges and return any issued obligation card.
steps: Check the account and return all materials.
Settle charges and any remaining obligations.
Confirm your clearance with the Library.
clearance.note: After graduation, the account may remain active for one year as an on-site-only graduate account.

research.label: Build a reading list
research.title: Do not begin a literature review with an empty search box
research.summary: The Library can prepare a thematic bibliography for a thesis or research project. Describe the topic, scope and expected source types.
steps: Define the topic, keywords and date range.
Send a request through the bibliography service.
Review the list and retrieve sources from the catalogue or databases.
research.note: The list is a starting point for your own source assessment, not a substitute for critical literature review.

copyRouter.label: Item router
copyRouter.heading: The catalogue found it. What next?
copyRouter.lead: A search result should not end with a call number. Choose the location from the record to see the real route into your hands.
copyRouter.locationLegend: Which location is shown in the catalogue?

magazine.title: Order online and wait for confirmation
steps: Order the closed-stack item in the catalogue.
Choose the Circulation Desk or Book Locker.
Wait for an email confirming preparation.
Collect the order within 4 days.
magazine.result: The Book Locker works 24/7 and is pickup-only. Do not travel before the message arrives.

open.title: Go to the floor and find the call number
steps: Save the floor number and call number.
Find the section, then the call-number position on the shelf.
Borrow through Selfcheck or ask a librarian.
open.result: You do not need to order an open-shelf book while the Library is open.

closed.title: Order from the floor for later pickup
steps: Choose the item on the correct floor in the catalogue.
Order it to the Circulation Desk or Book Locker.
Wait for email and collect within 4 days.
closed.result: Ordering floor items becomes available outside Library opening hours.

onsite.title: Use the item inside the Library
steps: Save the location and call number.
Find the item or ask a librarian.
Use it in the designated space.
onsite.result: A red marking means on-site use only — the item cannot leave the Library.

floors.label: Floor compass
floors.heading: Your subject points to a floor
floors.lead: Colours from the Infopack become a spatial map. Always confirm the final location in the particular item's record.

one.title: Floor 1 · green
one.mood: Conversation, group work and general collections

activation.label: working days to activate an account after online registration

always.label: Book Locker for pickup and return box for returns

studentMattersLive.metaDesc: See whether to start with the Dean’s Office, a USOS application, a vice-dean or the Dean, and find the right person for your programme.
studentMattersLive.heroLabel: Start with the matter, not the organisation chart.
studentMattersLive.heroLead: Most matters begin at the Dean’s Office, not with a message to the most senior person. Choose what you need and we will show the right sequence, person and information to prepare.

source.label: Service path
source.title: Infopack “Information from the Dean and Vice-Deans”

router.heading: What brings you here?
router.lead: The router follows the Infopack rule: information and service at the Dean’s Office first, then the appropriate procedure, and contact with a vice-dean only when the earlier level did not resolve the matter.
router.rule: Do not send the same matter to several people in parallel. Keep the contact sequence and describe what has already been agreed.
router.ariaLabel: Choose the type of student matter

information.label: I need information or advice
information.title: Start with the adviser for your programme at the Dean’s Office
information.summary: Dean’s Office staff are assigned by programme, cycle, year and study mode. This is the right first place to verify a procedure, deadline, whether an application is appropriate, and required attachments.
steps: Find the current adviser for your programme.
Ask one specific question and state your study details.
Record the answer or arrangements before taking the next step.
prepare: Programme, cycle, year and study mode
Student number if needed for identification
A one-sentence description of the result you need

certificate.label: I need a certificate
certificate.title: Certificates and confirmations are handled by the Dean’s Office
certificate.summary: You do not need a vice-dean appointment for this. Confirm the document type, request method, preparation time and collection method with your programme adviser.
steps: State the exact name and purpose of the certificate.
Contact the adviser for your programme.
Confirm when and how the document can be collected.
prepare: Required language and any data scope
External deadline, if one has been set

documents.label: I want to submit or collect documents
documents.title: Transfer documents according to the Dean’s Office instructions
documents.summary: Your programme adviser will confirm the place, opening hours and acceptable delivery form. For application attachments, provide legible, complete and credible scans.
steps: Check current opening hours and the correct room.
Confirm whether an electronic version is sufficient.
Keep proof of submission or collection.
prepare: A complete document set without alterations
Legible scans with signature and stamp where required
Case number or message to which the document relates

application.label: I know I need an application
application.title: Use the Applications Compass, not a random email
application.summary: When you have USOS access, applications are submitted through the system. The Compass helps choose the type, deadline, reasons, attachments and legal basis.
steps: Choose your situation in the Applications Compass.
Check the deadline and all required attachments.
Submit the right USOS application and monitor its status.
prepare: A precise request — exactly what you want to obtain
Factual reasons if that application requires them

unresolved.label: The Dean’s Office did not solve my problem
unresolved.title: Only now take the matter to the appropriate Vice-Dean
unresolved.summary: Contact a vice-dean when the Dean’s Office could not provide information or a solution, confirmed that an application is not the right route, or the vice-dean asked you to make contact.
steps: Find the vice-dean assigned to your programme.
Begin by stating exactly what result you need.
Describe the problem, earlier Dean’s Office contact and attach evidence.
prepare: Date and channel of Dean’s Office contact
The answer received or information that there was no solution
Documents and an unambiguously named expected result

summons.label: I was summoned or the matter was escalated
summons.title: Reply through the channel and by the deadline in the summons
summons.summary: The Dean handles specified formal matters and those referred to that level. Do not ignore the summons or independently change the contact route.
steps: Read the full summons and record the deadline.
Collect every requested explanation and document.
Reply via the requested channel; if unsure, confirm the method with the Dean’s Office.
prepare: A complete answer to every point
Documents in the form and by the deadline specified by the University

programme.label: Current responsibility map
programme.heading: Who is responsible for your programme?
programme.lead: The search uses the current UEW structure checked on 13 August 2026. Enter part of the Polish or English programme name.
programme.hint: Enter at least two characters. The Dean handles, among others, finance/accounting programmes and management; the others cover their assigned programme groups.
programme.noResult: We did not find the programme in the current map.

message.label: Escalation without chaos
message.heading: A message that can be acted on
message.lead: The Infopack identifies four elements of good contact with a vice-dean: a concrete objective, the problem, earlier Dean’s Office arrangements and documents.
message.subject: Message framework to complete
message.template:
Subject: [programme, year] — [short case name]

Dear Dean / Vice-Dean,

decision.heading: What has just happened to you?

prepare.label: I am preparing for assessments or exams
prepare.title: Pass the class components before sitting the exam
prepare.summary: Passing every other component of the course is required for admission to the exam. A negative grade at the first attempt gives you a resit, but a positive exam grade cannot be improved.
prepare.signal: Control-test dates should be announced at least 2 weeks ahead, and exam dates no later than 4 weeks before the session.
actions: Review the requirements given during the first class.
Compare the exam timetable with all component assessments.
After every grade, check whether you are entitled to a resit.
checks: No more than four exams in one semester.
An unexcused absence results in a 2.0 grade.
One negative component grade makes the final course grade negative.

absence.label: I missed an assessment or exam
absence.moment: the reason and a quick response matter
absence.title: An excused absence opens the way to an individual date
absence.summary: Give the teacher the reason and documents within 14 days, or the examiner within 3 days after the reason ends. If accepted, an individual date can be set.
absence.signal: If the new date falls after the relevant session ends, the Dean’s consent is required.
actions: Record the date on which the reason for your absence ended.
Send the explanation and evidence to the teacher or examiner.
If the date falls outside the session, submit a reasoned application to the Dean.
checks: The document supports a significant reason for the absence.
The message reached the right person on time.
You have a confirmed new date or instructions for an application.

missing.label: A grade is missing or incorrect
missing.title: Teacher first; after three working days, the Dean’s Office
missing.summary: You must verify final grades within 7 days after the resit session. Report a missing or inconsistent grade immediately to the teacher, who has up to 3 working days to correct it.
missing.signal: A missing entry is not the same as a failing grade — start the correction procedure first.
actions: Take a screenshot of the grade or empty field and record the date.
Write to the teacher with the course, group and correct grade.
If there is no entry or correction after 3 working days, notify the Dean’s Office.
checks: You are checking the final course grade, not only a component.
You have proof that the first report was sent.
Do not request conditional progression until every grade is entered in USOS.

dispute.label: I believe the grade is unfair
dispute.moment: after a first-attempt or resit grade is announced
dispute.title: A committee is not a third attempt — identify a concrete flaw
dispute.summary: The application may concern impartiality, inconsistency with the rules or scope given in the first class, or the conduct of the assessment or exam. The committee’s grade is final.
dispute.signal: A negative committee grade rules out conditional progression; requesting repetition of the semester remains possible.
actions: Record the exact date the disputed grade was announced.
Collect the requirements, your work and facts about the process.
Submit a detailed application within 2 working days.
checks: Your reasons describe a procedural concern, not only disappointment with the result.
You know that the committee chair decides the form.
You may nominate your own observer.

failed.label: I failed a course or the semester
failed.moment: after all entries and the resit session
failed.title: Conditional progression and repetition are different decisions — both require an application
failed.summary: Conditional progression lets you continue while repeating failed courses if the Dean considers the ECTS deficit not excessive. Repeating the semester may also involve programme differences.
failed.signal: Apply only after every grade is entered in USOS, but no later than 10 days after the resit session. No justification is required.
actions: Check all grades and list failed courses with their ECTS.
Compare conditional progression with repeating the semester; the Dean decides eligibility.
Submit the correct USOS application, then verify the date, courses and fee in the decision.
checks: A negative committee result rules out conditional progression.
Repeating the first semester of first-cycle studies exceptionally requires the Rector’s consent.
Check the current fee in the order applicable to your cohort, not in an old PDF.

where.q: Where do I submit a scholarship application?
where.a: You print every benefit application from your student account in the USOSweb system. You submit the signed application together with the required documentation at the Student Service Office.

when.q: When will the scholarship be paid?
when.a: Payment requires collecting the decision in the USOSweb system. Decision notifications are sent to your university email address.

multiple.q: Can I receive several benefits at once?
multiple.a: Yes. For example, the disability scholarship is independent of income and can be combined with other benefits. The details are set out in the scholarship benefits regulations.

firstTime.q: I’m applying for a social scholarship for the first time — what should I remember?
firstTime.a: Attach an income declaration and full documentation confirming your family’s income. If you have an adult sibling who is studying, attach a current certificate of continued education.

diff.q: How does a hardship grant differ from a social scholarship?
diff.a: A hardship grant is one-off help in a sudden, temporarily difficult life event, awarded independently of the social scholarship.

If your family does not receive social assistance, the scholarship is still possible once you document how the family supports itself (Section 16(4) and (5) of the Regulations).

You then count only your own, your spouse’s and your children’s income.

deklaracja.metaDesc: Digital accessibility statement for the SSUEW Student Government website — WCAG 2.1 conformance, the complaints procedure and contact details.
deklaracja.heroLead: The Student Government of Wrocław University of Economics and Business is committed to the digital accessibility of this site in line with the Polish Digital Accessibility Act of 4 April 2019.
deklaracja.metaDate: Statement prepared on: 26 June 2026. Last reviewed: 30 July 2026. Method: self-assessment by the public body, supported by an automated tool (axe-core) and a code review.
deklaracja.intro: The site is designed to WCAG 2.1 level AA, and in many places AAA: sufficient contrast, visible focus, full keyboard support, semantic headings, text alternatives and respect for reduced-motion preferences.

sections.title: Conformance status
sections.body: The site is partially conformant with the Digital Accessibility Act — it meets WCAG 2.1 level AA within the scope covered by the audit carried out. The audit of 30 July 2026 combined automated testing (45/45 axe-core scans, zero violations) with a code review (contrast, keyboard operation and focus, semantics, forms, touch targets ≥ 44 px); every issue found was fixed. Exclusions — elements not yet verified: (1) how the site is experienced through a screen reader (an NVDA/VoiceOver session is planned — automated tests and code review do not replace it), (2) the accessibility of PDF documents and photo alt texts that will be published on the site in future. Each of these will undergo a separate accessibility review, and this statement will be updated accordingly.

sections.title: Keyboard support & aids
sections.body: You can navigate the site with the keyboard (Tab / Shift+Tab, Enter, Esc). A “skip to content” link, clearly visible focus and a search opened with Ctrl/⌘ + K are available. The site respects the system reduced-motion setting (prefers-reduced-motion) and works in light and dark mode.

sections.title: Feedback and complaints procedure
sections.body: Anyone has the right to request that the website or an element of it be made accessible. Send your request to kontakt@samorzad.ue.wroc.pl, indicating the page concerned and a convenient form of contact. If accessibility cannot be ensured, we will propose alternative access. If a request is refused, you may file a complaint with the supervising authority and a petition to the Ombudsman.

sections.title: Architectural accessibility
sections.body: Student Government office: ul. Kamienna 44, Building L, room 110, 53-307 Wrocław. Detailed information about the building’s architectural accessibility (entrance, lifts, parking, access for assistance-dog users) is available on request — write to kontakt@samorzad.ue.wroc.pl.

prywatnosc.metaDesc: How the SSUEW Student Government processes data on this site — contact form, analytics, cookies and your rights (GDPR).
prywatnosc.heroLead: We explain what data we process on this site, why, and what rights you have.

sections.title: Data controller
sections.body: The data controller is the Student Government of Wrocław University of Economics and Business, ul. Kamienna 44, 53-307 Wrocław. For data matters, write to: kontakt@samorzad.ue.wroc.pl.

sections.title: What data we process
sections.body: Site forms (contact, Student Ombudsman, partnerships): your name or organisation name, email address and message — solely to respond to your enquiry. Submissions go to a Google Sheet and to the Student Government mailbox within the University’s Google account — no external form relay is involved. Member login uses a Google account in the @samorzad.ue.wroc.pl domain; we only store a technical session in a necessary cookie.

sections.title: Data processors
sections.body: Our forms are handled by a Google Apps Script running on the Student Government account inside the University’s Google Workspace. A submission is stored in a Google Sheet and delivered to the mailbox belonging to that form. The Student Government remains the controller; Google acts as a processor under the agreement held by the University. Only the content you type into the form reaches the script. The Student Ombudsman form may concern sensitive matters — those submissions go to a separate mailbox, and if you would rather skip the form entirely, write directly to rps@samorzad.ue.wroc.pl. The site is hosted on Vercel (Vercel Inc.), which processes the server logs necessary to operate it.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.body: Necessary cookies (a logged-in member’s session and your language preference) always work — they are required for the site to function. Analytics cookies and scripts run only with your consent; you can change your choice at any time by clearing the site’s data in your browser.

sections.title: Analytics
sections.body: We use Vercel Web Analytics — anonymous, aggregated visit statistics. It uses no cookies and does not identify individuals. We collect it only if you consent.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You have the right to access, rectify, erase or restrict the processing of your data, as well as the right to object and to lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority (in Poland: the President of the Personal Data Protection Office). We keep contact-form data only as long as needed to handle your case.

sections.title: Contact
sections.body: Send privacy and data questions to: kontakt@samorzad.ue.wroc.pl.

wydawnictwo.heroLead: A paper from a course or a research circle can become a real publication — with an ISBN and open access. The bar is lower than you think.
wydawnictwo.aboutIntro: Debiuty Studenckie is a series published by the Wrocław University of Economics and Business Press — a publisher operating since 1955 that puts out more than 100 titles a year. The series is addressed directly to student research circles: a place where a paper, article, or chapter written in a circle can become a real publication.

years.title: Year I or II is enough
years.desc: The authors are first- and second-year students. You don't need to wait for your master's thesis or have a research track record — a text worth showing is enough.

license.title: CC BY-SA 4.0 — no hidden barriers
license.desc: Every publication is released in open access under a Creative Commons licence. You can freely share it, cite it, and build on it.

layout.title: Layout and an ISBN

publish.title: Publication in open access
publish.desc: The finished publication is released in open access under CC BY-SA 4.0 — available to everyone, free of charge.
